user.title: What manages your network?
user.description: Pick your router or controller. If it isn't listed, choose Network scan.

unifi.title: Ubiquiti UniFi
unifi.description: UniFi OS consoles (UDM, UDR, UCG, UX, Cloud Key Gen2+) use port 443; self-hosted controllers use 8443. Use a local admin account (View Only is enough), not a ui.com account with 2FA.

omada.title: TP-Link Omada
omada.description: Hardware controllers (OC200/OC300/OC400) use port 443; the Software Controller uses 8043. Use a local controller account (Viewer is enough).

asus.title: ASUS router
asus.description: Works with stock ASUSWRT and Asuswrt-Merlin, including AiMesh. Use the router's admin login. Turn on HTTPS if the web UI only allows HTTPS (usually port 8443). Shows WiFi, band and channel, but ASUS does not report per-device traffic.

fritzbox.title: AVM FRITZ!Box
fritzbox.description: Requires 'Allow access for applications' under Home Network → Network → Network Settings. Use a FRITZ!Box user (leave the username empty if you log in with password only). Per-device traffic is not available.

openwrt.title: OpenWrt
openwrt.description: Requires LuCI (installed by default). Log in as root. WiFi, channel and live activity are read from this router's own access points.

mikrotik.title: MikroTik RouterOS
mikrotik.description: RouterOS 7.1+ with the www (port 80) or www-ssl (port 443) service enabled. A read-only user is enough. Live activity comes from WiFi registration counters, and from Kid Control if you use it.

opnsense.title: OPNsense
opnsense.description: Create an API key under System → Access → Users (edit your user → API keys). Enter the key as the username and the secret as the password.

scan.title: Network scan (any router)
scan.description: Works with any router. Home Assistant probes the subnet and reads its ARP table, giving name, MAC, vendor and IP. WiFi, channel and activity need one of the router options instead. Home Assistant must be on the same network (Home Assistant OS, or Docker with host networking).

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate
reauth_confirm.description: The login stopped working. Enter the current credentials.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect. Check the host, port, HTTPS setting and site.
error.invalid_subnet: Enter valid subnets like 192.168.1.0/24 (4096 addresses at most).

data.swap_direction: Swap upload/download (enable if they look reversed)
